reasoning: Both sets plan all six stages with serious quant rigor: hand-built estimators checked against references, walk-forward evaluation, purged folds, within-date shuffle nulls, logged attempts, sealed holdouts, and paper-only trading. A wins clearly on content. It routes every chance test to the null-hypothesis-testing skill by name at the step where the test happens (WALK-08, SCREEN-02, INCR-05, FCMP-02, TCMP-03, AD-12/15/18/24/29). It follows the user's stage plan closely: stage-5 inputs are the stage-4 survivors, and every stage-6 candidate is tested against the stage-3 classical portfolios. It is also tighter. Its weaknesses are real, though. Holdout dates are stale across the ideas files and the architecture overview. Global out-of-scope lines ('deep learning', 'Machine-learning portfolio methods') contradict stages 5-6. The PPO is described with 'six sleeves' but lists five. WALK-01 runs to the last complete month despite the HOLD rules. The trading holdout covers only about nine months. B is weaker on content. It hand-builds its testing protocol (QR-10) and names the skill only for the stage-2 test design, never at the stage-4/5/6 test steps. It deliberately does not build stage 5 on the stage-4 survivors, and its agent claims are not tested against the stage-3 portfolios directly. It also carries much more residue: tombstoned goals, '(changed …)' notes on almost every Serves line, about 40 '(confirmed)' assumptions, duplicated out-of-scope lines, and stale goal and stage references. Its quant design is at least as careful in places, though: exposure-matched baselines for agents that hold cash, a true-covariance oracle, BH then Holm corrections, curated final returns, and the honest admission that only forward paper trading is left for stage 6. B is also much easier to navigate. The spec has per-stage sections and definitions, each stage has its own architecture doc with a one-paragraph overview, and plan.md lays out a concrete Stage 1 milestone plan. A has a single 1,000-line architecture file, run-on summaries and no build plan. Under the rubric's equal weighting of the content and structure means, B's structure lead slightly outweighs A's content lead.

strengths: Every chance test is handed to the null-hypothesis-testing skill by name, with statistic, null, sidedness and correction family spelled out (WALK-08, SCREEN-02, INCR-05, FCMP-02, TCMP-03)
Follows the user's stage plan closely: stage 5 uses the features that survived stage 4 (NN-04), and stage-6 candidates are tested against the best stage-3 classical portfolio (TCMP-02)
Strong guardrails: placebo, relabelling and planted-signal checks; simulated GARCH; random and perfect-foresight allocators; a hand-built network and PPO checked against PyTorch and SB3
Worked numeric examples check out (WALK-08's 21+39 comparisons, SIM-02's 40% move, SIM-03's 0.005%, PPO-03's 0.019, FLOG-03's 42)
History from 2005 includes 2008; T-bill cash; costs at 2/5/10 bps; a clear laptop-first GPU rule within a $45 total budget
weaknesses: No build plan or milestone order, so the next build step has to be inferred from AD-03 and the CLI
The architecture is one 1,000-line file, and the spec has no stage headings; stages are found only by requirement prefix
Stale holdout text in two ideas files and the architecture overview; out-of-scope lines contradict stages 5-6
WALK-01 runs the stage-2/3 study to the last complete month, while HOLD-01/06/08 forbid any study from reading locked dates
The trading holdout runs only from 2026-01 to the freeze (about 9 months), too short for a Sharpe-difference test to have power
History residue: about 20 '(changed 2026-10-15)' tags, the superseded AD-19 stub, a merged-idea stub, and 'Brief changes' sections in every idea

strengths: Clear per-stage organization: stage-sectioned spec with its own definitions, a system architecture map plus one doc per stage, each with an 'in one paragraph' overview
plan.md gives an ordered Stage 1 milestone plan with done-when criteria and decision points (source probe first)
Learning-oriented: synthetic labs before real data (LAB, ORCL, FLAB, SYN5, PPOLAB) and notebooks that derive each method before its code

Careful quant design: curated final returns for delistings, residuals with loadings fixed at t, BH screen over all attempts then Holm on the holdout, and exposure-matched baselines so holding cash can't win the variance tests for free
Honest stage-6 design: no unseen history is left, so confirmation comes only from at least 24 months of forward paper trading on six pre-registered risk claims
weaknesses: The null-hypothesis-testing skill is not routed at stage-4/5/6 test steps; QR-10 makes the testing protocol hand-built, and the skill appears only for the stage-2 test design
Departs from the user's plan: stage 5 deliberately skips the stage-4 survivors, and agent claims R4-R6 are not tested against the stage-3 classical portfolios
Heavy residue: tombstoned goals 3/4/5/7/8, '(changed … Goal X merged)' on almost every Serves line, about 40 '(confirmed)' assumptions, and AD-24 kept in full
Many stale references across the ideas and architecture files (retired goals, the '~3 years' holdout, Stage 4-5-only seal, AD-21 import contract)
Committed history starts in 2011, so 2008 is only in the stretch period; stage-6 cash earns 0%
About 40% longer than A, with optional add-ons (SECT, TWIN, HRPV, LADR, 11 notebooks) that inflate the plan
